topic.title: Statistical Models of Neural Spiking and Population Activity
topic.overview: Neural recordings contain discrete spikes, variable counts, and partially observed population dynamics. This cluster develops probabilistic spike models, latent dynamical systems, and differentiable simulators to connect those observations with circuit behavior. It examines which statistics a fitted model must reproduce to be a credible account of the recorded activity.
topic.whyItMatters: High likelihood alone may not yield realistic simulated neural behavior. Hidden neurons and mismatched variability can distort inferred connectivity, so models need checks on population statistics and dynamics as well as prediction fit.
topic.evolution: Early representatives study cell assemblies, receptive fields, and Bayesian signal classification. Later work adds integrate-and-fire estimation and low-dimensional count dynamics. Recent examples fit summary statistics through stochastic simulation and pursue large-scale biophysical models, while some adjacent work transfers spiking mechanisms into robust sensory processing.
openQuestions: Which summary statistics distinguish realistic circuits from merely good predictive fits?
How can uncertainty about unobserved neurons be carried into connectivity or stimulation conclusions?
